# Stage 2 plan — a season from start to finish

The goal and exit test are in the [build order](../specs/v1/technical/T10-build-order.md), stage 2: part A is the demo cut, then the TCSAAL demo milestone, then part B and the exit test. This file breaks the stage into steps small enough for one builder each. Each step says what it needs; any step whose needs have landed can be opened beside the others. How to do a step is in the [runbook](RUNBOOK.md).

## What this machine can and cannot do

- **Node 24 and git are here. Docker, the Supabase command-line tool and the GitHub command-line tool are not.** Do not try to install them.
- **The local database is PGlite**, real PostgreSQL running inside Node, already a dependency of this repository. Migrations, row-level security and every database test run against it. The same SQL must also run on Supabase's PostgreSQL later, so use nothing PGlite-only.
- **There are no vendor accounts yet.** Every outside service sits behind an interface in `packages/providers` with a local stand-in. The real adapter is written and unit-tested against recorded responses, and marked "not verified against the live service" until the founder supplies an account. That list goes into the stage report.
- **No live push service here.** Supabase Realtime cannot be reached. Live game updates run through a local stand-in inside the web app (server-sent events) behind the same interface the Supabase adapter will use. How many viewers the real service carries is measured only in staging.
- **No page cache service here.** Cloudflare's "clear by label" is behind an interface with a local stand-in; whether our plan includes it is checked when the account exists (T5 §4).
- **No real phones or tablets.** The tracker is tested in a real browser on this computer, with phone-sized screens, the connection cut on purpose and the tab closed mid-game. Testing on real hardware (T-190) and the rehearsal game are the founder's.
- **No real data, ever (T-201).** Al-Hadi's recorded games live in the founder's hosted database and Faraj's history in Faraj's. Neither may be contacted. `supabase/site.json` names the real Al-Hadi project: nothing in the gate and nothing a run does may reach it. The Faraj project at `../faraj-league` may be read for the shape of its tables (its `supabase/migrations/` files) and nothing else: never its seed files, exports or data. Both transfers are built and tested against made-up files shaped like the real ones.
- **The Al-Hadi tracker keeps running untouched** until this stage passes its exit test (T-213, T-16). Nothing here changes `apps/live-stats` or how it behaves. The tracker rebuilt in the web app is new code beside it, reusing the engine in `packages/sports`.

## Steps

Each step is done when its done test passes, the gate passes, the independent review is closed, and it is committed. "Isolation case" means the command or query is registered in the two-league harness of steps 1.9 and 1.10, so league A's access is tried against league B's records on every run. Page steps take their text from message files (T-187), build every league address with the one address builder (T-34), pass the accessibility checks (T-186), work at phone width (A-2), add short help text where the screen needs it (A-10), and handle the states every screen must (T-184, A-4): nothing here yet, an error that says so and keeps what was typed, and no permission (2.105 audit, finding L6). Since 2026-11-14 a page step is also looked at before it lands: its builder takes its look from the shared display pieces and classes and adds none of its own, its screens are photographed with `node scripts/shots.mjs`, and a design reviewer checks the pictures against [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) (runbook, section 4).

### A. Tables for a season (part A)

Part A, the demo cut. These four migrations build on each other, so they land in order; the lead reserves each one's number when it opens.

- [x] **2.1 Divisions, venues, courts and settings tables.** A migration adds `divisions` (season, name, color, sort, parent division), `venues` and `courts` (a court belongs to a venue), and one table for setting values set at league, program or season level. T3 does not say where settings are stored: the lead records the choice and adds the table to T3 in the same change (T-185). Every table follows T-40 to T-47, gets its one forced row-level security policy (step 1.7), and the generated schema types are made again. _Spec: T3 §1, §4 and §12; T5 §6; T-40 to T-47, T-61. Needs: nothing new. Migration: yes. Folders: `supabase/migrations`, `packages/database/src/schema`, `packages/database/src/db`. Done test: a constraint test for each rule; as the app role with league A set, league B's rows are invisible and cannot be written; the harness snapshots the new tables. Model: opus, high._
- [x] **2.2 People, teams and rosters tables.** A migration adds `people` (a person as one league knows them, with an empty profile link until claimed), `teams` (season, division, short name, name, color, who sees its players' numbers, lineage) and `roster_entries` (jersey number, role, joined and left dates, sort). Role grants and invitations get their link to a real team, so a coach or captain grant points at a team in the same league. Seasons gain a real column for "jersey numbers must be unique in a team" (T-44), and the database refuses a duplicate number on one team while it is on. Team logos wait for uploads in stage 3, as season logos do. _Spec: T3 §3, §4, §5, §7 and §12; R-3, R-17; T-40, T-47. Needs: 2.1. Migration: yes. Folders: `supabase/migrations`, `packages/database/src/schema`, `packages/database/src/db`. Done test: a roster entry pointing at another league's team or person is refused by the database; a duplicate jersey is refused only when the season asks; the harness snapshots the new tables. Model: opus, high._
- [x] **2.3 Schedule and game tables.** A migration adds `rounds`, `stages` (one regular-season stage per season for now), `games`, `schedule_drafts`, `schedule_revisions`, `game_assignments` and `game_corrections`. The database enforces T3 §12: a game's two teams differ and belong to its season, a final game has both scores and a scheduled one has none. `games` carries `version`, its recording mode and `format`, the rules it started with. Corrections are history: never edited or deleted. _Spec: T3 §8 and §12; T-45, T-46, T-47; S-7. Needs: 2.2. Migration: yes. Folders: `supabase/migrations`, `packages/database/src/schema`, `packages/database/src/db`. Done test: a constraint test for each rule; a correction row cannot be changed or deleted; isolation of the new tables proven as in 2.1. Model: opus, high._
- [x] **2.4 Live game, calculated and import tables.** A migration adds `scoring_sessions`, `game_events` (every tap, never edited, each command ID and sequence number once per game), `game_states`, `player_game_stats`, the calculated `standings_rows`, `standings_adjustments` and `season_player_totals`, and `imports` (kind, status, report, and what it created so it can be undone). Roster entries gain a mark for a player added at the scorer's table (S-6); T3 is silent on where that flag lives, so the lead adds it to T3. The shapes follow the current tracker's tables so Al-Hadi's games carry over (T3 §8). _Spec: T3 §8, §9, §11 and §12; T6 §1; S-6. Needs: 2.3. Migration: yes. Folders: `supabase/migrations`, `packages/database/src/schema`, `packages/database/src/db`. Done test: the same command ID twice in one game is refused by the database; an event row cannot be changed; isolation of the new tables proven as in 2.1. Model: opus, high._

### F. Live games on the server (part A)

Part A. Scorekeepers, the one-scorer rule, the tracker's door and live updates.

Who may score a game follows the league's setting: any scorekeeper, or only those assigned (P4 §4); owners and admins always may. Roles are read from the database on every request (T-75). A query lists a scorekeeper's games for today and the week. _Spec: P4 §4; P7 §5.1; T6 §2; T-74, T-75. Needs: 2.3, 2.13, 2.14. Migration: no. Folders: `packages/core/src/modules/games`, `packages/database/src/queries`, `packages/database/src/stores`. Done test: under each setting, an assigned and an unassigned scorekeeper are allowed or refused correctly; a revoked role is refused at once; isolation cases. Model: opus, high._
- [x] **2.28 Scoring sessions and takeover.** Opening a game to score takes a lease held by one account and one device, renewed while the tracker is open and lapsing after about two minutes (T-116). A second scorekeeper sees who holds it and can take over after confirming; the first device's commands are refused from then on. Leaving the game releases it. _Spec: T6 §5; S-5; T-116. Needs: 2.4, 2.27. Migration: no. Folders: `packages/core/src/modules/games`, `packages/database/src/queries`, `packages/database/src/stores`. A command already taken is recognized by its ID and answered "duplicate"; a refused one gets its reason (T-113). Starting a game turns its season's rules into the engine's rules and the game keeps them (S-1). Commands from a session that no longer holds the game are refused, and the previous protocol version is still accepted (T-127). _Spec: T6 §1, §3 and §11; T-110 to T-113, T-127; S-1, S-5. Needs: 1.26, 2.6, 2.15, 2.28. Migration: no. Folders: `packages/core/src/modules/games`, `packages/database/src/queries`, `packages/database/src/stores`. ## Side by side

Lanes follow the runbook, section 3. A step can be opened once everything in its "Needs" has landed. The waves below are the earliest each step can open; everything in one wave may be open together, and the "Lanes" line in `STATUS.md` decides how many actually run. Prefer part A when lanes are scarce: the demo date depends on it.

Three rules on top of "Needs":

- **Migrations.** 2.1 to 2.4 build on each other and land in order; the lead reserves each number at opening. None is open beside a stage 1 step that changes the same tables: step 2.2 changes `role_grants`, `invitations` and `seasons`, so it waits if step 1.12 is changing those.
- **Fence, sign-in, sessions and permissions.** 2.13, 2.27, 2.28, 2.32, 2.33 and 2.46 may be built side by side where their "Needs" allow, each in its own lane. Each gets an opus reviewer, and they land one at a time like every lane.
- **The engine.** 2.66, 2.67 and 2.123 are the only steps that change `packages/sports/src/basketball`; never open two at once, and open none while step 1.26 or a later catch-up with `main` is still open.
- **The look.** 2.85 is opened ahead of every other stage 2 step (the founder, 2026-11-14) and is built by the design lead ([DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md)). 2.102 and 2.103 open side by side once it lands. While 2.85 is open, a lane that changes a public page takes the build branch in again after 2.85 lands and before its own design review, so its screen is judged in the new look.
- **Area audits.** Steps 2.105 to 2.111 are the area leads' audits ([LEADS.md](LEADS.md)). At most two are open at once, in number order after 2.85, and each writes only its own file under `docs/build/audits`, so an audit never clashes with a building lane. Steps 2.35 to 2.38 (the scoring screens) are built on `fable` against 2.107's checklist; since 2.107 landed (2026-11-14) they wait for the steps it added that their "Needs" name: 2.35 opens alone once 2.33, 2.113, 2.122 and the courtside look in DESIGN.md are in, and 2.36 and 2.37 open side by side when it lands. An audit's High findings become the next steps opened in its area, ahead of new features: for 2.107 those are 2.117 to 2.121; for 2.105 they are 2.125, 2.126 and 2.127, with 2.126 landed before the statistics and team parts of 2.93 and 2.127 before 2.102. After them, 2.128, 2.137, 2.139 and 2.140 open first: they are small and cost more with every page built (2.105 audit, section 7).

## Needs the founder

Everything up to these points is built and tested here with made-up data. Each is in plain words, with the step it belongs to.

- **What the demo league calls itself (F-10, step 2.60).** Decided for you on November 13, 2026, as recommended: the demo league carries an "unofficial demo, not run by TCSAAL" notice, uses no TCSAAL logo and stays out of search until TCSAAL agrees. Step 2.60 no longer waits. Say so if you want it different: both are league settings.
- **Two-step sign-in on the business accounts (T-83).** Due before this stage puts real accounts into production: about twenty minutes in each vendor's settings.
- **Vendor accounts for a real demo.** The demo must run somewhere other people can open, so it needs the Supabase, Render, Cloudflare and Resend accounts and a domain from stage 1's checklist. Then the live updates adapter (step 2.31) and the cache adapter (step 2.26) are checked against the real services, and how many live viewers the plan allows is measured.
- **The transfer of Al-Hadi's recorded games (F-7, steps 2.57 and 2.58).** The real games are in your hosted database, which no AI session may touch (T-201). You, or a session you supervise with no AI access to the data, make the backup with `npm run stats:copy` and run the transfer into the demo league; the runner's report must show every box score line matching.
- **The demo league's real content (F-6, step 2.59).** Someone gathers every TCSAAL varsity boys team, its fixtures and results from TCSAAL's public site into the import template: a few hours, repeated as results come in. Other schools' rosters only where TCSAAL already shows them; their players' statistics stay staff only.
- **Al-Hadi's staff (F-6).** Inviting the real coach and scorekeepers to their roles, with their own accounts in place of the passcode.
- **The rehearsal and the real game (the milestone, T-123, T-190).** A full rehearsal game scored on real phones and tablets, including a bad Wi-Fi test, then a real game scored on the platform. The current tracker keeps running throughout (T-213), so for the first real game we suggest scoring it in both, with two scorekeepers, and comparing.
- **Booking the TCSAAL meeting (F-4).** For after Al-Hadi's season, not for its last game (T10, "Timing").
- **The transfer of Faraj's history (steps 2.78 to 2.80).** You export Faraj's tables (Faraj's own export, or one file per table from its database) and run the transfer into an unpublished league. The check compares against the export; you then compare a few teams and players with the live Faraj site by eye.
- **Faraj seasons with totals but no game-by-game numbers, if there are any.** The platform calculates totals from games (A-12, S-9). If an old season holds players' season totals with no per-game lines behind them, the transfer will list them, and you will be asked how they should appear. This is a question for later, not a blocker.
- **Fuller statistics for Al-Hadi (T-215).** If Al-Hadi's coaches want rebounds and assists this season, say so: it adds about a week of steps to this plan.
- **Not in this stage, for awareness.** Placeholders that only admins see on an empty unpublished site (O-1, decided for you on November 13) are not built here: empty pages say "nothing here yet" to everyone. A team's coach choosing who sees the team's numbers from their own tools comes with stage 4; in this stage an admin sets it.
